title: Move a String
description: Show that assigning a String moves ownership so the original name cannot be used.

explanation.overview: String is not Copy. Passing it into take moves the value; first is gone after the call.

keyTerms.definition: Transfer of ownership. The old binding cannot be used.
Types like i32 duplicate on assignment. String does not.

explanation.howItWorks: take receives ownership of the heap buffer. After the call, first is uninitialized from the compiler's point of view, so using it would not compile.
explanation.designPattern: Pass ownership when the callee should free the value; borrow when the caller still needs it.

quiz.question: What happens to first after take(first)?
options: It is moved and cannot be used
quiz.explanation: String assignment and pass-by-value move ownership.

quiz.question: How would you keep using first after the call?
quiz.explanation: Clone duplicates, or change the signature to borrow.

quiz.question: Why is i32 different?
quiz.explanation: Copy types are duplicated instead of moved.

title: Shared Borrow
description: Read a String through &str without taking ownership.

explanation.overview: &str is a borrowed view. shout never owns name, so main can print both values.

keyTerms.definition: A &T that lets many readers and no writers.
A string slice: pointer plus length into UTF-8.

explanation.howItWorks: &name coerces to &str. to_uppercase allocates a new String for the result.
explanation.designPattern: Prefer &str in APIs so callers can pass String or literals.

quiz.question: Does shout free name?
quiz.explanation: It borrowed; the owner is still main.

quiz.question: What does &name become?
quiz.explanation: Deref coercion turns &String into &str.

quiz.question: How many shared borrows of name are allowed at once?
quiz.explanation: Many &T are allowed; they cannot overlap a &mut T.

title: Exclusive Borrow
description: Mutate a String through one &mut at a time.

explanation.overview: A &mut T is exclusive. While it is live, no other borrow of that value may exist.

keyTerms.definition: One &mut T; no overlapping readers or writers.
The owner must be mut to lend a &mut.

explanation.howItWorks: greeting is mut. push_bang appends through the exclusive borrow, then the borrow ends and println can read.
explanation.designPattern: Keep &mut scopes short so later reads compile.

quiz.question: Why must greeting be mut?
quiz.explanation: Only a mut owner can create an exclusive borrow.

quiz.question: Could you print greeting while push_bang holds &mut?
quiz.explanation: Shared and exclusive borrows cannot overlap.

quiz.question: What does push append?
quiz.explanation: String::push takes a char.

title: Named Lifetime
description: Return the longer of two string slices with an explicit lifetime.

explanation.overview: The returned slice cannot outlive either input. 'a names that shared region.

keyTerms.definition: A name the compiler uses to check borrows, not a runtime value.
Rules that fill in lifetimes in common cases. This signature needs an explicit one.

explanation.howItWorks: Both inputs and the output share 'a, so the result is valid as long as both inputs are.
explanation.designPattern: When a function returns a reference derived from arguments, name the relationship.

quiz.question: Is 'a a runtime value?
quiz.explanation: Lifetimes are erased at runtime.

quiz.question: Why not return a String instead?
options: You can; this version avoids allocation
quiz.explanation: Owned String would drop the lifetime puzzle at the cost of an alloc.

quiz.question: What does the output borrow?
quiz.explanation: It returns a or b.

title: Option unwrap_or
description: Provide a default when a map lookup returns None.

explanation.overview: HashMap::get yields Option<&V>. copied turns Option<&i32> into Option<i32> so unwrap_or can supply 0.

keyTerms.definition: Some(T) or None. Forces you to handle absence.
Maps Option<&T> to Option<T> when T: Copy.

explanation.howItWorks: "b" is missing, so get is None, copied stays None, unwrap_or returns 0.
explanation.designPattern: Prefer unwrap_or / unwrap_or_else over unwrap in library code.

quiz.question: What does score_of print for "b"?
quiz.explanation: Missing keys become 0.

quiz.question: Why call copied?
quiz.explanation: copied lifts the reference so the default can be i32.

quiz.question: What is unwrap on None?
quiz.explanation: unwrap panics when the Option is None.

title: Propagate Result
description: Parse an integer and bubble errors with the ? operator.

explanation.overview: ? returns early on Err, otherwise unwraps the Ok payload. The function signature must be compatible.

keyTerms.definition: Ok(T) or Err(E). Recoverable failure.
Early-return operator for Result and Option.

explanation.howItWorks: "9".parse() succeeds. ? yields 9, then Ok(10) is returned.
explanation.designPattern: Use ? in fallible pipelines; match or map_err at the boundary.

quiz.question: What does parse_plus_one("9") return?
quiz.explanation: Parse 9 then add one.

quiz.question: What does ? do on Err?
options: Returns the Err from this function
quiz.explanation: ? propagates the error.

quiz.question: Could this function return i32 instead?
quiz.explanation: unwrap would panic on bad input; Result is the honest API.

title: Implement a Trait
description: Give a custom type a Display impl.

explanation.overview: Display is the trait behind {}. Implementing it lets println format your type.

keyTerms.definition: A set of methods a type can implement.
User-facing formatting, as opposed to Debug {:?}.

explanation.howItWorks: write! forwards to the formatter. println! looks up Display for Point.
explanation.designPattern: Implement Display for humans, Debug for developers.

quiz.question: Which placeholder uses Display?
quiz.explanation: {} is Display.

quiz.question: What does fmt return?
quiz.explanation: Formatting can fail; Result signals that.

quiz.question: Is Display automatically derived?
options: No, you implement or skip it
quiz.explanation: Debug can be derived; Display is manual.

title: Iterator Adapter
description: Filter and map a slice into a collected Vec.

explanation.overview: Adapters are lazy. collect forces the pipeline into a Vec.

keyTerms.definition: filter/map/etc. that wrap another iterator.
Turn an iterator into a collection via FromIterator.

explanation.howItWorks: 2 and 4 pass the filter, then become 3 and 5.
explanation.designPattern: Prefer iterator chains over indexed loops when they stay readable.

quiz.question: What is printed?
quiz.explanation: Even values 2 and 4 plus one.

quiz.question: When does filter run?
quiz.explanation: Adapters are lazy.

quiz.question: What does iter() yield?
quiz.explanation: slice::iter yields shared references.

title: HashMap Entry
description: Count tokens with the entry API instead of double lookup.

explanation.overview: entry returns Occupied or Vacant. or_insert(0) inserts once, then you increment in place.

keyTerms.definition: A view of a key that may or may not exist yet.
Insert a default if vacant; return a &mut to the value.

explanation.howItWorks: "be" is seen twice, so the count becomes 2.
explanation.designPattern: Use entry to avoid get-then-insert races in sequential code and extra hashing.

quiz.question: What is map["be"]?
quiz.explanation: Two occurrences of be.

quiz.question: What does or_insert return?
quiz.explanation: A mutable reference to the stored count.

quiz.question: Why to_string on the key?
quiz.explanation: The map stores owned String keys.

title: Match an Enum
description: Branch on a custom enum without panicking on unknown variants.

explanation.overview: match must cover every variant. Binding name and n extracts payload.

keyTerms.definition: A type that is one of several variants, optionally with data.
The compiler rejects a match that misses a variant.

explanation.howItWorks: Token::Number(7) matches the second arm and formats num 7.
explanation.designPattern: Prefer match over if-let chains when every variant matters.

quiz.question: What is printed?
quiz.explanation: The Number arm runs.

quiz.question: What if you omit Token::Eof?
quiz.explanation: Matches must be exhaustive.

quiz.question: Is Token Copy?
quiz.explanation: String is not Copy, so the enum is not Copy.

title: Drop Guard
description: Run cleanup when a value goes out of scope.

explanation.overview: Drop runs when the owner is dropped. RAII ties cleanup to scope, even on early return.

keyTerms.definition: Trait whose drop method runs at the end of a value's life.
Resource Acquisition Is Initialization: release in Drop.

explanation.howItWorks: _g ends at the inner block, drop sets done to true, then println sees true.
explanation.designPattern: Put locks, files, and spans in types that unlock/close on Drop.

quiz.question: What is printed?
quiz.explanation: Drop flipped the flag.

quiz.question: When does drop run here?
options: At the end of the inner block
quiz.explanation: The binding _g is dropped when the block ends.

quiz.question: Does mem::forget run Drop?
quiz.explanation: forget leaks on purpose and skips Drop.

title: Arc Mutex Counter
description: Share a counter across threads with Arc<Mutex<T>>.

explanation.overview: Arc shares ownership across threads. Mutex serializes mutation. clone on Arc bumps the refcount.

keyTerms.definition: Atomically reference-counted pointer, Send + Sync when T is.
Mutual exclusion lock around interior mutability.

explanation.howItWorks: Three threads each add one. After join, the mutex holds 3.
explanation.designPattern: Arc<Mutex<T>> for shared mutable state; channels when you can avoid sharing.

quiz.question: What is printed?
quiz.explanation: Three increments under the lock.

quiz.question: Why Arc::clone instead of moving counter?
options: Each thread needs its own Arc handle
quiz.explanation: The original Arc must remain in main for the final read.

quiz.question: What does lock().unwrap() do on a poisoned mutex?
quiz.explanation: unwrap turns a poison error into a panic.

title: mpsc Channel
description: Send values from a worker thread over a channel.

explanation.overview: mpsc is multiple-producer, single-consumer. send moves the value to the receiver.

keyTerms.definition: A queue that moves messages between threads.
Blocks until a message arrives or the senders drop.

explanation.howItWorks: The worker sends 41. main recv's it and prints 42.
explanation.designPattern: Prefer message passing when threads should not share memory.

quiz.question: What is printed?
quiz.explanation: 41 plus one.

quiz.question: Why move the sender into spawn?
options: Sender is not Clone in this snippet
quiz.explanation: This example moves the only sender; clone tx for multiple producers.

quiz.question: What if all senders drop before recv?
quiz.explanation: Disconnected channel: recv errors.

title: Cow Str
description: Borrow when possible and allocate only when mutation is needed.

explanation.overview: Cow is clone-on-write: Borrowed until you need an owned clone to mutate.

keyTerms.definition: Enum of Borrowed or Owned for the same data type.
Delay allocation until a write happens.

explanation.howItWorks: "ok" stays borrowed. "a b" needs replace, so it returns an owned String.
explanation.designPattern: Return Cow when some inputs need allocation and others do not.

quiz.question: Does normalize("ok") allocate a String?
quiz.explanation: No spaces, so Cow::Borrowed.

quiz.question: What does replace return?
quiz.explanation: str::replace always allocates a new String.

quiz.question: Why the lifetime on Cow<'_, str>?
quiz.explanation: The borrowed variant is tied to input.

title: Recursive Box
description: Store a recursive enum variant behind Box so the type has a known size.

explanation.overview: A type cannot contain itself inline (infinite size). Box breaks the cycle with a heap pointer.

keyTerms.definition: Owned heap allocation with a known pointer size.
A type that mentions itself in a variant or field.

explanation.howItWorks: sum walks Cons cells until Nil. 1+2+0 = 3.
explanation.designPattern: Box (or Rc/Arc) for recursive data; Vec for most sequences.

quiz.question: Why Box around List?
options: So List has a finite size
quiz.explanation: Indirection makes the enum sized.

quiz.question: Is Box<List> the same as &List?
options: No, Box owns the heap value
quiz.explanation: Box is owned; &List is a borrow.

title: Trait Bound
description: Write a generic function that works for any Display type.

explanation.overview: T: Display means any type that implements Display. Monomorphization builds a copy per type.

keyTerms.definition: A constraint on a generic type parameter.
Codegen of a specialized copy per concrete type.

explanation.howItWorks: label(7) uses i32's Display. label("ok") uses &str's Display.
explanation.designPattern: Bound generics on the behavior you need, not on a pile of concrete types.

quiz.question: Could label accept a type without Display?
quiz.explanation: format! needs Display.

quiz.question: Is T inferred?
quiz.explanation: The compiler infers T from the call.

quiz.question: What does format! return?
quiz.explanation: format! allocates a String.
